FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Sports Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production and General Engineering Division 
Council. 


As the performance of a weight lifter is dependent largely on the equipment he uses and the equipment that is made 
available in competitions, formulation of a national standard was considered very essential. 


This standard was first published in 1968. This revision has been taken up to keep pace with the latest technological 
developments, international practices, and technical rules and regulations of the International Weightlifting 
Federation. In this revision, the following major changes have been made: 


a) Collar specifications are incorporated; 

b) Requirements of discs have been updated; 

c) Performance test method has been updated; and 

d) Specifications for barbell set for women are incorporated. 


The composition of the Committee, responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 
2022 “Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)”. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 4630 : 2022 


Indian Standard 
BARBELL SET — SPECIFICATION 
( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements for barbell set 
used in a weightlifting competition. 


2 REQUIREMENTS 


The barbell set consists of the following parts: 
2.1 Bars 


2.1.1 The bars shall be made from chromed steel, 
machined with knurling in grip section and capable of 
satisfying the performance test given in 4. The bars are 
further classified as given below: 


a) Men Bar, weight 20 ke" HÄ percent; and 
b) Women Bar, weight 15 kg*9:12 percent. 


2.1.2 Dimensions for the men’s bar shall be as given 
in Fig. 1 and the dimensions for the women’s bar shall 
be as given in Fig. 2. Tolerances on dimensions for 


both men and women bar shall be ee percent. 


2.2 Discs 


2.2.1 The discs can be made from mild steel, plastics, 
or cast iron. Discs having weight of more than 10 kg 
shall be covered with rubber or plastics. Discs are 
classified as competition discs and training discs. The 
discs shall conform to the requirements as mentioned 
in Table 1. Both sides of the discs shall be coated with 
a permanent colour. 


2.2.2 The competition discs shall be coloured wholly 
on both the sides as per column 5 of Table 1. 


2.2.3 Training discs shall be either coloured wholly 
with the corresponding colour as given in column 5 of 
Table 1 or full black colour with a rim of the 
corresponding colour as per column 5 of Table 1, and 
marked as ‘Training’. 


2.2.4 The tolerances on the weight of competition 
discs shall be as given in Table 1 whereas the 
tolerances on the weight of training discs shall be + 0.8 
percent. 


2.3 Collar 


For holding the discs on the bar, each bar shall be 
equipped with two collars. The collar shall be made 
from chromed steel. The collars shall meet the 
requirements as given in Table 2. 


3 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


The bar shall be comfortable to hold in hands and the 
discs shall be free from casting defects. All the sharp 
edges shall be rounded off. The chromed plating shall 
be free from pin-holes, cracks, and such other defects 
which may impair its serviceability. 


4 PERFORMANCE TEST 


The bar with all the discs in position, weighing 
approximately 190 kg shall be lifted to a height of 2.5 
metres and dropped free on the ground normally used 
for weight lifting. After completion of the test, the bar 
or any disc shall show no sign of cracking or 
permanent deformation. 


5 PACKING AND MARKING 
5.1 Packing 


The barbell set shall be packed as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier. 


5.2 Marking 


5.2.1 Each bar and disc/package shall be marked with 
the followings: 


a) Manufacturer’s name; 
b) Identification mark or registered trade-mark; and 
c) Marked with its weight in kilograms. 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Mark 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this 
standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 


may be marked with the Standard Mark.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PGD 41(17575).
